info.title: WppFy -  WhatsApp API
info.description:
API for managing WhatsApp instances and communications.

## Important Recommendation: WhatsApp Business
**It is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to use WhatsApp Business accounts** instead of regular WhatsApp for integration; regular WhatsApp may present inconsistencies, disconnections, limitations, and instability when used with our API.

## Authentication
- Regular endpoints require a 'token' header with the instance token

## Instance States
Instances can be in the following states:
- `disconnected`: Disconnected from WhatsApp
- `connecting`: Connection in progress
- `connected`: Successfully connected and authenticated

id.description: Opaque identifier generated by the server. Do not assume UUID format.

isBusiness.description: Indicates whether it is a business account

current_presence.description: Current presence status of the instance (non-persisted field)

lastDisconnect.description: Textual date/time of the last disconnection

chatbot_stopMinutes.description: How long the chatbot will stay paused when using stop conversation

chatbot_stopWhenYouSendMsg.description: How long the conversation will stay paused when you send a message manually

fieldsMap.description: Map of the instance's custom fields (when present)

currentTime.description: Current time returned by the API

created.description: Creation date returned by the API. Treat the value as text; the format may vary.

updated.description: Last update date returned by the API. Treat the value as text; the format may vary.

Chat.description: Represents a conversation/ticket in the system

id.description: Unique conversation ID (r + 7 random bytes in hex)

wa_archived.description: Indicates whether the chat is archived

wa_contactName.description: Name saved in the phone's address book for this number (empty: not saved). The conversation is created with it (by LID, via the linked number) and it changes when the contact is saved or deleted on the phone.

wa_name.description:
Name set by the user in the WhatsApp profile ("push name").
Comes from the contact's profile and may not be available depending on the context or data source.

name.description:
Name resolved by the system as a fallback.
It usually consolidates the best value available among internal data, the name coming from WhatsApp and the name saved in contacts.
Therefore, it is more likely to be filled in.

parent_community.description: Parent community of the chat when it represents a subgroup

wa_isBlocked.description: Indicates whether the contact is blocked

wa_isGroup.description: Indicates whether it is a group

wa_isGroup_admin.description: Indicates whether the user is a group admin

wa_isGroup_announce.description: Indicates whether it is an announcement-only group

wa_isGroup_community.description: Indicates whether it is a community

wa_isGroup_member.description: Indicates whether is a group member

wa_isPinned.description: Indicates whether the chat is pinned

wa_notes.description: Internal chat notes synced via app state

lead_awaitingReply.description: `true` when the contact is awaiting a reply: the last message is theirs and no one has resolved the conversation (`POST /lead/resolve`). The contact's message turns it on; ours (you, the AI, a flow, or an integration) turns it off. In conversations predating this field, the api decides based on the sender (the instance's number or LID). Only in conversations with people: absent in groups and channels, which are not included in either filter, and when the conversation has no known last message (only the date). Filterable in `/chat/find`.

wa_muteEndTime.description: Timestamp of the end of muting

common_groups.description: Groups in common separated by commas, format: (group_name)group_id

lead_tags.description:
Lead tags. Tags configured with `kanban=true` also determine the
columns in which the card appears in the Kanban.

lead_isTicketOpen.description: Indicates whether there is an open ticket

chatbot_agentResetMemoryAt.description: AI memory start (ms): the agent only reads the conversation messages from this point on. 0: no cutoff (the agent's window applies). Set via `/chat/editLead`.

chatbot_lastTrigger_id.description: ID of the last executed trigger

chatbot_disableUntil.description: Automation (AI, triggers, and flows) paused in this conversation until this time, in milliseconds. `-1`: until someone turns it back on; `0`: on.

chatbot_summary.description: Reason for the pause made by the automation: human request (AI or flow; paused until someone turns it back on) or AI reply limit (1-hour pause). Empty when there is no pause or after it ends. Turning it back on (`chatbot_disableUntil: 0` in `/chat/editLead`) or resolving (`POST /lead/resolve`) clears it.

Message.description: Represents a message exchanged in the system

id.description: Internal unique message ID (format r + 7 random hex characters)

messageid.description: Original message ID at the provider

isGroup.description: Indicates whether it is a group message

fromMe.description: Indicates whether the message was sent by the user

status.description:
Message lifecycle status.
Common examples: `Queued`, `Canceled`, `Failed`, `Sent`, `Delivered`, `Read`.
In group messages, it follows the most advanced participant: `Delivered` when at least one received it, `Read` when at least one read it, and `Played` when at least one listened to it.

convertOptions.description: Conversion of message options, list, poll and buttons

buttonOrListid.description: ID of the selected button or list item

content.description: Raw message content (serialized JSON or text)

wasSentByApi.description: Indicates whether the message was sent via API

pinned.description: Message pinned in the conversation (pin and unpin also arrive in `messages_update`, types `Pinned` and `Unpinned`)

sendFunction.description: Function used to send the message (when sent via API)

sendPayload.description: Payload used in the send when available. Base64 media data is omitted.

callPeer.description: Known contact associated with a call, when available in `messageType: call`.

send_folder_id.description: Folder associated with the send (when applicable)

ai_metadata.description: Record of an AI round. The full one (request to the model, response, and `outcome`) is stored once, on the contact's last message that the round replied to, even when nothing went out (error, discarded response). Each message sent by the AI carries only `agent_id` and `turn` (the `id` of that contact message).

agent_id.description: ID of the responsible AI agent

turn.description: In the message sent by the AI: the `id` of the contact's message where the full record of the round is stored.

flow_id.description: Message sent by a flow: the flow's `id`. A message sent by the AI includes the `agent_id`.

request.description: Request data for the AI API

messages.description: History of messages sent to the API

outcome.description: What the round actually did (only in the full record).

status.description: `sent`: something was sent; `cancelled`: discarded (the conversation was paused, a flow started, or the hourly reply limit was reached); `error`: the provider failed; `empty`: nothing to send.

handoff.description: `chamar_humano`: the summary for whoever takes over.

lead.description: `atualizar_lead`: what was written to the CRM (`lead_email = ana@exemplo.com; column = Agendado`).

detail.description: Why it was discarded, or the error.

sender_image_preview_url.description: Temporary preview URL of the sender, when known. Hydration in this version fills in messages received in groups; the field may be omitted. It does not trigger a photo query to WhatsApp during listing.

Label.description: Represents a label/category in the system

id.description: Unique label ID

colorHex.description: Hexadecimal color corresponding to the index

NameSetAt.description: Date of the last name change

NameSetBy.description: JID of the user who set the name

NameSetByPN.description: LID/PN of who set the name

TopicSetAt.description: Date of the last description change

TopicSetBy.description: JID of who changed the description

TopicSetByPN.description: LID/PN of who changed the description

TopicDeleted.description: Indicates whether the description was deleted

IsLocked.description:
Indicates whether only administrators can edit group info
- true = only admins can edit
- false = everyone can edit

IsAnnounce.description: Indicates whether only administrators can send messages

DisappearingTimer.description: Time in seconds for messages to disappear

IsIncognito.description: Indicates whether the group is incognito

IsParent.description: Indicates whether it is a parent group (community)

IsJoinApprovalRequired.description: Indicates whether approval is required for new members

IsDefaultSubGroup.description: Indicates whether it is a default subgroup of the community

Participants.description: List of participants. It is null when omitted by noParticipants and may be empty when participant_profiles is present.

OwnerCanSendMessage.description: Checks whether you are able to send messages

OwnerIsAdmin.description: Indicates confirmed administrator privilege. May be absent when false; partial data does not grant administrator privilege.

DefaultSubGroupId.description: If the current group is a community, this field shows the ID of the announcements subgroup

invite_link.description: Invite link, exposed only to admins with confirmed permission. May be absent; do not assume every read queries WhatsApp.

request_participants.description: Known join requests, comma-separated. Exposed only to administrators when requested.

image_url.description: URL of the already persisted full image; the API does not query WhatsApp during listing

image_preview_url.description: URL of the already persisted preview

picture_id.description: Identifier of the full image on WhatsApp

picture_empty_at.description: Last confirmation that the group had no image

parent_community.description: Summary of a subgroup's parent community

participant_profiles.description: Additional participant profiles, when available. Missing fields must not be inferred.

items.description: Additional profile of a participant; missing fields must not be inferred.

ParticipantCount.description: Known number of participants. May differ from the list size when data is partial or has been omitted from the response.

request_participants_lid.description: LIDs of known join requests, comma-separated; admin only, when requested.

IsSuperAdmin.description: Indicates whether is a super administrator

DisplayName.description: Name displayed or resolved locally for the participant

ImagePreview.description: Legacy field not populated. Use participant_profiles[].image_preview_url.

Username.description: Username observed on WhatsApp, when available.

price.description: Value in thousandths of the currency (19990 = R$ 19.99).

shortCut.description: Shortcut to find the reply (and what the AI uses to choose).

aiDescription.description: Reserved for automated support. Empty by default.

onWhatsApp.description: Whether the reply is also in WhatsApp Business (text only).

QuickReplyItemInput.description: On creation, `shortCut` and `message` are required. On edit, only the fields sent change; `message` replaces the entire message.

shortCut.description: Shortcut to find the reply (and what the AI uses to choose).

aiDescription.description: Reserved for automated support. Empty by default.

onWhatsApp.description: Only on creation and only with `kind: text`: also creates it in WhatsApp Business.

ApiError.description: Standard error for the new routes. `code` is stable and is meant for handling the error in code; `error` is the human-readable message and may change.

code.description: Stable error code, such as `validation_failed` or `not_found`.

LeadTag.description:
Lead tag. When `kanban=true`, the record also defines a column of the
instance's Kanban.

id.description: Opaque, stable ID generated by the system

kanban.description: Indicates whether the tag appears as an active column in the Kanban

kanbanOrder.description: Column ascending order in the Kanban

created.description: Creation date. Textual value from the record; may use YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.SSSZ.

updated.description: Last update date. Textual value from the record; may use YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.SSSZ.

QuickReplyMessage.description:
Stored message: `kind` plus the same body as the corresponding send, without `number` and without send fields (`replyid`, `mentions`, `delay`, `readchat`, `readmessages`, `async`, `forward`, `track_source`, `track_id`).

| kind | Body same as | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `text` | Accepts placeholders such as `{{name}}`. |
| `media` | [`/send/media`](/endpoint/post/send~media): `type`, `file`, `text`, `docName` | `type`: image, video, document, audio, ptt or myaudio. A `file` by URL is kept as sent; in base64, it is stored by the API (image 5 MB, audio and video 16 MB, document 20 MB; 50 MB per instance). |
| `contact` | [`/send/contact`](/endpoint/post/send~contact) | `fullName` and `phoneNumber` required. |
| `location` | [`/send/location`](/endpoint/post/send~location) | `latitude` and `longitude` required. |
| `menu` | [`/send/menu`](/endpoint/post/send~menu) | `type`: button, button_legacy, list or poll (carousel not yet). The button media (`file`) only by URL. The options must be sendable, otherwise `400`: poll with at least 2, list with at least one item (a `[...]` section does not count) and buttons with at least 1. |
| `pix` | [`/send/pix-button`](/endpoint/post/send~pix-button) | `pixType` and `pixKey` required. |

AuthError.description: Authentication error, the same for all routes: `code` is the HTTP status.

OffsetPagination.description: Pagination by `limit`/`offset`. For the next page, repeat the call with `offset = nextOffset` while `hasMore` is `true`.

offset.description: Position of the first item on the page.

hasMore.description: Whether there are more items after this page.

InternalError.description: Unexpected failure while writing or reading the data.

QuickReplyConflict.description: Conflict with the state of the instance or the reply. `instance_not_paired`: the instance has not yet been connected to WhatsApp; connect it first. `instance_not_connected`: a WhatsApp Business reply (`onWhatsApp`) can only be created, edited or deleted while the instance is connected. `conflict` (edit only): another edit changed the message at the same time; nothing was saved, read the reply again and retry.

NotFound.description: No resource with this `id` on this instance.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request. `invalid_body`: malformed JSON or unknown field. `validation_failed`: value outside the allowed range.

InstanceNotPaired.description: The instance has not yet been connected to WhatsApp. The data belongs to the connected number; connect the instance first (`instance_not_paired`).

WhatsAppSyncFailed.description: The change did not reach WhatsApp Business (`whatsapp_sync_failed`). Only happens with `onWhatsApp` replies. Nothing was saved or deleted; try again.

tags.name: Proxy
tags.description:
WppFy uses an internal proxy by default.
You can keep this default, configure your own proxy via `proxy_url`, or use your Android phone as a proxy by installing the app from https://github.com/WppFy/silver_proxy_apk (direct APK: https://github.com/WppFy/silver_proxy_apk/raw/refs/heads/main/silver_proxy.apk).
If nothing is sent, we keep using the internal proxy. IPs are Brazilian; for international clients, consider a proxy in the client's region.

tags.name: Send Message
tags.description:
Endpoints for sending WhatsApp messages with different content types.

## Common Optional Fields

All message sending endpoints support the following optional fields:

- **`delay`** *(integer)*: Delay in milliseconds before sending
  - During the delay, "Typing..." or "Recording audio..." will appear depending on the type
  - Example: `5000` (5 seconds)

- **`readchat`** *(boolean)*: Mark chat as read after sending
  - Removes the unread message counter from the chat
  - Example: `true`

- **`readmessages`** *(boolean)*: Mark last received messages as read
  - Marks the last 10 **received** messages (not sent by you) as read
  - Useful to confirm reading pending messages before replying
  - Different from `readchat` which only removes the unread counter
  - Example: `true`

- **`replyid`** *(string)*: ID of the message to reply to
  - Creates a reply linked to the original message
  - Support varies by message type
  - Example: `"3A12345678901234567890123456789012"`

- **`mentions`** *(string)*: Numbers to mention (only for group sending)
  - Specific numbers: `"5511999999999,5511888888888"`
  - Mention all: `"all"`

- **`forward`** *(boolean)*: Marks the message as forwarded in WhatsApp
  - Adds the "Forwarded" indicator to the message
  - Example: `true`

- **`track_source`** *(string)*: Message tracking source
  - Identifies the system or source sending the message
  - Useful for integrations (e.g., "chatwoot", "crm", "chatbot")
  - Example: `"chatwoot"`

- **`track_id`** *(string)*: ID for message tracking
  - Free identifier to track the message in external systems
  - Allows correlating messages between different platforms
  - **Note**: The system accepts duplicate values - there is no uniqueness validation
  - Use the same ID in multiple messages if it makes sense for your integration
  - Example: `"msg_123456789"`

### Sending to Groups
- **`number`** *(string)*: To send a message to a group, use the group ID ending with `@g.us`
  - Example: `"120363012345678901@g.us"`
  - **How to get the Group ID:**
    - Use the `chatid` from the webhook received when someone sends a message in the group
    - Use the `GET /group/list` endpoint to list all groups and their IDs

## Available Placeholders

All message sending endpoints support dynamic placeholders for automatic personalization:

### Name Fields
- **`{{name}}`**: Consolidated chat name, using the first available option:
  1. Lead name (`lead_name`)
  2. Lead full name (`lead_fullName`)
  3. WhatsApp contact name (`wa_contactName`)
  4. WhatsApp profile name (`wa_name`)

- **`{{first_name}}`**: First valid word of the consolidated name (minimum 2 characters)

### WhatsApp Fields
- **`{{wa_name}}`**: WhatsApp profile name
- **`{{wa_contactName}}`**: Contact name as saved in WhatsApp

### Lead Fields
- **`{{lead_name}}`**: Lead name
- **`{{lead_fullName}}`**: Lead full name
- **`{{lead_personalid}}`**: Personal ID (SSN, CPF, CNPJ, etc)
- **`{{lead_email}}`**: Lead email
- **`{{lead_status}}`**: Current lead status
- **`{{lead_notes}}`**: Lead notes
- **`{{lead_assignedAttendant_id}}`**: ID of the assigned attendant

### Custom Fields
Fields added via custom fields are accessible using `{{lead_field01}}` to `{{lead_field20}}` or use `{{fieldname}}` defined in `/instance/updateFieldsMap`.

### Usage Example
```
Hello {{name}}! I saw you work at {{company}}.
Is your email {{lead_email}} correct?
```

**💡 Tip**: Use `/chat/find` to fetch chat data and see available fields before sending messages with placeholders.

tags.name: Async Message
tags.description:
Operational controls for the internal asynchronous send queue used when a send endpoint receives `async=true`.

This section is used to:
- check the current state of the async queue
- configure the delay between messages sent with `async=true`
- clear pending backlog and cancel messages not yet completed

Scope:
- covers only the internal queue of async direct messages
- does not change messages already sent successfully

tags.name: Newsletters and Channels
tags.description:
Operations for reading and following WhatsApp channels (newsletters).

Main use cases:
- list posts already published in a channel
- edit recent posts in a channel
- delete recent posts in a channel
- check post views and reactions
- integrate channels without needing to persist messages locally

Notes:
- `/newsletter/messages` returns the post content
- `/newsletter/messages/edit` edits the content of recent posts
- `/newsletter/messages/delete` deletes recent posts
- views (`viewsCount`) and reactions (`reactionCounts`) come in each post of `/newsletter/messages`, not via webhook event
- `/newsletter/updates` is deprecated: WhatsApp does not respond and the API returns 504
- newsletters use their own routes and must not use `/message/edit` or `/message/delete`

tags.name: Quick Replies
tags.description:
Management of quick replies to streamline service.

**⚠️ Important**: This feature is only useful if you use a custom frontend/interface
to register and use the replies. The API only stores the replies, 
but does not apply them automatically.

### How it works:
- **Create**: Register pre-defined responses with titles and content
- **List**: Retrieve all registered responses to display in your interface
- **Use**: Your frontend system can use these responses to speed up typing

### Use cases:
- Custom web service interfaces
- Mobile apps with reply suggestions
- CRM systems with message templates
- Productivity tools for attendants

**Not a chatbot**: For automatic responses, use Chatbot features.

tags.name: CRM
tags.description:
Complete customer relationship management system integrated with the API.

**💾 Internal Storage**: All lead data is saved directly in the API,
eliminating the need for external databases. Your application can focus only
on the interface and business logic.

### Available Features:
- **📋 20+ customizable fields**: Name, phone, email, company, notes, etc.
- **🏷️ Label System**: Organize and categorize your contacts
- **🔍 Advanced Search**: Filter by any field or label
- **📊 Complete History**: All interactions are registered automatically

### 🎯 Placeholders in messages:
Use dynamic variables in messages for automatic personalization:

```
Hello {{name}}! I saw you work at {{company}}.
Is your email {{email}} correct?
Notes: {{notes}}
```

### Typical Flow:
1. **Capture**: Leads arrive via WhatsApp or forms
2. **Enrichment**: Add data using `/chat/editLead`
3. **Segmentation**: Organize with labels
4. **Communication**: Send personalized messages with placeholders
5. **Follow-up**: History is saved automatically

**Ideal for**: Sales, marketing, support, lead qualification

tags.name: Chatwoot Integration
tags.description:
**🚧 BETA INTEGRATION - Chatwoot integration system for unified service**

**⚠️ WARNING**: This integration is in BETA phase. Use at your own risk. We recommend testing in a non-production environment before use in production.

This category contains resources to configure and manage integration with Chatwoot, an open-source customer service platform. The integration allows centralizing WhatsApp conversations in Chatwoot.

### Available Features:
- 🔧 **Complete Configuration**: Configure URL, tokens, and Chatwoot credentials
- 📬 **Bidirectional Sync**: New messages between WhatsApp and Chatwoot are synced automatically
- 📱 **Contact Management**: Automatic sync of names and phones
- 🔄 **LID→PN Update**: Automatic migration from Local ID to Phone Number
- 🏷️ **Smart Names**: Name system with tilde (~) for automatic update
- 🚫 **Group Separation**: Option to ignore groups in sync
- 👤 **Message Signature**: Agent identification in sent messages
- 🔗 **Automatic Webhook**: URL generated automatically to configure in Chatwoot

### 🏷️ Smart Name System:
- **Names with tilde (~)**: Updated automatically when contact modifies name in WhatsApp
- **Specific names**: For fixed name, remove tilde (~) from name in Chatwoot
- **Example**: "~John Doe" = automatic, "John Doe" = fixed
- **LID→PN Migration**: No conversation duplication during transition
- **Native responses**: Appear directly in Chatwoot without external markings

### ⚠️ Known Limitations:
- **History sync**: Not implemented - only new messages are synced

### Use Cases:
- Centralized service in Chatwoot
- Support teams with multiple agents
- CRM integration via Chatwoot
- Communication channel centralization
- Automatic contact and name management

**Ideal for**: Companies with service teams, call centers, technical support (in test environment)

**Requires**: Configured Chatwoot instance, API tokens, and test environment

**🚧 Remember**: BETA integration - features may change without prior notice

post.description:
Starts the instance's connection to WhatsApp.

- Without `phone`, returns a QR Code to scan with the phone.
- With `phone`, returns a pairing code for that number.

The instance remains in `connecting` until pairing is confirmed or the
timeout expires. Track progress via `GET /instance/status`; do not repeat the
call while the process is in progress.

After connecting, the available history starts arriving through the
`history` event and can be queried via `POST /message/find` and `POST /chat/find`.
The response may include `request_id` at the top level, even before the QR code
or pairing code is read. Keep this id to correlate the attempt with
the pairing's `history` batches, including the completion `status`, and with
`GET /instance/history-sync/status`. It stays the same during the same
attempt and changes with each new pairing. It may be absent when there is no
pairing or tracking available.

In a new pairing, `history_days` chooses how many days of history the
phone sends. Without the field, with a value outside 0–365, or from 1 to 90 days, the
request is the normal history (90 days, when there is no valid value). From 91
to 365 days, or with `0` (the maximum, 365 days), the request is the full
history, larger and slower. An already paired instance reconnects without
requesting history.

To choose a connection region, first query
`GET /proxy-managed/countries` and `GET /proxy-managed/cities` and reuse the
values returned in the `proxy_managed_*` fields.

phone.description: Phone number in international format (e.g., 5511999999999). If provided, generates a pairing code. If omitted, generates a QR code.

browser.description: Browser used in the authentication/connection cycle. `auto` keeps a valid saved profile or picks Safari, Firefox or Edge for new connections.

systemName.description: System/name displayed on the phone under linked devices. Helps identify the instance on WhatsApp; for greater stability, we recommend leaving it blank and using the default value of the chosen browser.

proxy_managed_country.description: Desired country for the regional proxy, in lowercase ISO alpha-2. Use the value returned by `GET /proxy-managed/countries`.

proxy_managed_state.description: State/subdivision of the chosen city. When the country/city requires disambiguation, use the `state` field returned by `GET /proxy-managed/cities?country=br`.

proxy_managed_city.description: City chosen for the regional proxy. Always use the `value` field returned by `GET /proxy-managed/cities`.

history_days.description:
Days of history requested from the phone during pairing.

- Absent: 90 days, via normal history.
- From `1` to `90`: the last N days, via normal history.
- From `91` to `365`: the last N days, via full history.
- `0`: the maximum, 365 days via full history.
- Outside 0–365: ignored; the 90 days apply.

Only applies to a new pairing. An already paired instance reconnects without
requesting history, and an already generated QR code or code keeps what was
requested. The phone decides what it sends: the days are a requested limit, not
a guarantee.

qr_code_brasil_com_proxy_regional.summary: QR code with regional proxy in Campinas/SP

codigo_com_um_ano_de_historico.summary: Pairing code requesting 1 year of history

jid.description: WhatsApp ID (when logged in)

request_id.description: Identifier of the pairing attempt and its initial history. Optional; it is the same one reported in the history events and in GET /instance/history-sync/status.

409.description: A connection flow is already in progress for the instance

Retry-After.description: Recommended time, in seconds, before retrying.

post.description:
Disconnects the currently connected WhatsApp account, ending the current session.
This operation:

- Ends the active connection

- Requires a new QR code to reconnect


Differences between disconnecting and hibernating:

- Disconnect: Completely ends the session, requiring a new login

- Hibernate: Keeps the session active, only pauses the connection


Use this endpoint to:

1. Completely end a session

2. Force a new authentication

3. Clear the current session's credentials

4. Restart the connection process


Possible states after disconnecting:

- `disconnected`: Disconnected from WhatsApp

- `connecting`: Reconnecting (after using /instance/connect)

info.example: The device has been successfully disconnected from WhatsApp. A new QR code will be required for the next connection.

post.description:
Requests a controlled resumption of the connection without deleting the instance or the
existing pairing. Use when the session is stuck or sends are not
progressing.

Possible behaviors:
- starts a new reset when the instance is eligible
- reports that a reset is already in progress
- reports that there is an active cooldown between resets
- returns an error when the session cannot be recovered or when the
  reconnection policy blocks the operation

The response includes:
- `instanceId`: ID of the authenticated instance
- `resetting`: whether a reset is currently in progress
- `queuedRecoveryAttempted`: whether pending messages were also included in the recovery attempt

200.description: Reset accepted, already in progress, or in cooldown

401.description: Invalid or missing token, or client not found

403.description: Reset blocked by the reconnection policy

409.description: Current session cannot be reconnected by reset

get.description:
Returns the current status of an instance, including:
- Connection state
- Updated QR code (if connecting)
- Pairing code (if available)
- Information about the last disconnection
- Full instance details

This endpoint is particularly useful for:
1. Monitoring connection progress
2. Getting updated QR codes during the connection process
3. Checking the current state of the instance
4. Identifying connection problems

Possible states:
- `disconnected`: Disconnected from WhatsApp
- `connecting`: Connecting (waiting for QR code or pairing code)
- `connected`: Successfully connected and authenticated

- `effective_mode` reports the connection in use: `custom`, `internal` or `direct`.
- `fallback.active` indicates that the main route is not available.
- `proxy_url` returns the configured URL with masked credentials.
- `last_test_error` helps diagnose the last known failure.

Under normal conditions, `mode` and `effective_mode` match. During a
contingency, they may diverge without changing the saved preference. Do not use
this endpoint for continuous polling; also monitor `GET /instance/status`.

post.description:
Explicitly sets one of the three accepted states:
  - `mode=custom`: uses your own proxy provided in `proxy_url`;
  - `mode=internal`: uses the internal infrastructure; or
  - `mode=none`: direct connection, allowed only with `confirm_no_proxy=true`.

Important: `POST /instance/proxy` confirms that the configuration was saved, not that the proxy has already been proven to be in use.
The main operational validation happens in the instance's next real connection cycle.

In practical terms:
  - `200 OK` here = configuration persisted successfully;
  - real connectivity failures may appear later; and
  - to observe the real state, query `GET /instance/proxy` and read:
    - `effective_mode`
    - `effective_detail`
    - `fallback.active`
    - `last_test_error`
    - `validation_error`

When `mode=custom`, you can also define the fallback via `proxy_fallback`:
  - `internal`: tries the internal infrastructure and, if it still fails, may use direct as a last resort;
  - `never`: does not use a fallback; or
  - a fallback proxy URL controlled by the client.

When `mode=internal`, `rotate_now: true` immediately replaces the persisted internal proxy.
If more than one internal source is available, the platform picks another source without exposing the provider.
If there is only one source, it only swaps the proxy/IP within that source.

Protocols accepted in custom proxy URLs:
  - `http://usuario:senha@host:porta`
  - `https://usuario:senha@host:porta`
  - `socks5://usuario:senha@host:porta`
  - `socks5h://usuario:senha@host:porta`

The generic `socks://` scheme is not accepted. For SOCKS proxies, use `socks5://` or `socks5h://`.

Accepts `internal`, `never`, or a fallback proxy URL using `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://`, or `socks5h://`.

The values returned in `countries[].value` are exactly those accepted in

get.description:
Returns the list of cities available for use in the
`proxy_managed_country`, `proxy_managed_state` and `proxy_managed_city` fields of the
`POST /instance/connect` endpoints.

Successful responses send `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`. If the
city catalog is temporarily unavailable, try again
after the interval indicated in the response.

- Authentication: public endpoint, no `token`.
- Protection: limit of 120 requests per minute per IP; exceeding it returns `429` with `Retry-After`.
- Query `country` (optional): lowercase ISO alpha-2. Default `br`.
- Query `state` (optional): lowercase state/subdivision, such as `sp`.
- Query `search` (optional): partial filter by name/slug, accent- and case-insensitive.

How to choose the city:
1. Use `br` in `proxy_managed_country`.
2. Call `GET /proxy-managed/cities?country=br` to get the Brazilian cities.
3. When the city returns `state`, also send that value in `proxy_managed_state`.
4. When the user chooses a city, send in `/instance/connect`:
   - `proxy_managed_country`: the chosen country, e.g. `br`
   - `proxy_managed_state`: the `state` returned by the city, e.g. `sp`, when available
   - `proxy_managed_city`: always `cities[].value`

If `state` is not present in the selected city, send only `proxy_managed_country` and `proxy_managed_city`.
The API validates the combination and returns an error if any required data is missing.

Request example:
```
GET /proxy-managed/cities?country=br&state=sp&search=camp
```

post.description:
Sends a text message to a contact, group, or channel/newsletter.

## Specific Features

- **Link previews** with support for automatic or custom personalization
- **Basic text formatting**
- **Automatic replacement of dynamic placeholders**

## Sending to a Newsletter

To send text to a channel, use the same `number` field, but provide the full channel JID:
- Example: `120363123456789012@newsletter`

```json
{
  "number": "120363123456789012@newsletter",
  "text": "Post publicado no canal"
}
```

## Replying to a poll, list, or button

Use this same endpoint to reply to an interactive message that is
stored in the instance's local history. Send:

- `number`: chat where the original message was received or sent;
- `replyid`: ID of the original interactive message;
- `text`: selection starting with `>`.

The `>` marker is required to generate an interactive reply. Without it,
the API only sends a text message quoting the original.

### Replying to a poll

Use the option's position, starting at 1. In this public documentation,
reply to only one option per request.

```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "replyid": "3EB0ID_DA_ENQUETE",
  "text": ">1"
}
```

### Replying to a list

Prefer the `rowId` configured when creating the list. The exact text
of the item or its position (`>1`) is also accepted.

```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "replyid": "3EB0ID_DA_LISTA",
  "text": ">plano_pro"
}
```

### Replying to a button

Prefer the quick reply button ID. The exact displayed text or its
position (`>1`) is also accepted. This applies to legacy quick buttons,
templates, native flow, and carousel. URL, call, or copy buttons perform
their own action and are not replied to through this flow.

```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "replyid": "3EB0ID_DOS_BOTOES",
  "text": ">confirmar"
}
```

The API returns an error when the original message is not available or the
provided option does not exist.

## Common Fields

This endpoint supports all **common optional fields** documented in the **"Send Message"** tag, including:
`delay`, `readchat`, `readmessages`, `replyid`, `mentions`, `forward`, `track_source`, `track_id`, placeholders, and sending to groups.

## Link Previews

### Automatic Preview
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "text": "Confira: https://exemplo.com",
  "linkPreview": true
}
```

### Custom Preview
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "text": "Confira nosso site! https://exemplo.com",
  "linkPreview": true,
  "linkPreviewTitle": "Título Personalizado",
  "linkPreviewDescription": "Uma descrição personalizada do link",
  "linkPreviewImage": "https://exemplo.com/imagem.jpg",
  "linkPreviewLarge": true
}
```

number.description: ID of the chat the message will be sent to. Can be a phone number in international format, a group ID (`@g.us`), a user ID (with `@s.whatsapp.net` or `@lid`) or a channel/newsletter ID (`@newsletter`).

text.description: Message text. To reply to a poll, list, or button, use a selection starting with `>` together with `replyid`. Accepts placeholders in regular text messages.

linkPreview.description:
Enables/disables link previews. If true, automatically looks for a link in the text to generate a preview.

Behavior:
- If only linkPreview=true: generates an automatic preview of the first link found in the text
- If custom fields are provided (title, description, image): uses the provided values
- If custom fields are partial: combines them with automatic link data as fallback
- Title or description containing only whitespace: the preview is generated without that field, without fetching from the link

post.description:
Sends different types of media to a contact, group or channel/newsletter. Supports URLs or base64 files.

## Supported Media Types
- **`image`**: Images (JPG preferably)
- **`video`**: Videos (MP4 only)
- **`videoplay`**: Video with autoplay/loop visual behavior on WhatsApp
- **`document`**: Documents (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, etc)
- **`audio`**: Regular audio (MP3 or OGG)
- **`myaudio`**: Voice message (alternative to PTT)
- **`ptt`**: Voice message (Push-to-Talk)
- **`ptv`**: Video message (Push-to-Video)
- **`sticker`**: Sticker

## Specific Features
- **Upload via URL or base64**
- Optional **caption** with placeholder support
- **Custom name** for documents (`docName`)
- **Automatic thumbnail generation for images and videos** when `thumbnail` is not provided
- **Optimized compression** according to the type
- **`viewOnce`** recommended for compatible media

## Sending to Newsletter

To send media to a channel, use the same `number` field, but provide the channel's full JID:
- Example: `120363123456789012@newsletter`

```json
{
  "number": "120363123456789012@newsletter",
  "type": "image",
  "file": "https://exemplo.com/foto.jpg",
  "text": "Imagem publicada no canal"
}
```

## Common Fields

This endpoint supports all the **common optional fields** documented in the **"Enviar Mensagem"** tag, including:
`delay`, `readchat`, `readmessages`, `replyid`, `mentions`, `forward`, `track_source`, `track_id`, placeholders and sending to groups.

## Basic Examples

## View Once (`viewOnce`)

The `viewOnce` field is recommended when you want view-once media and currently takes effect for the types:
`image`, `video`, `videoplay`, `ptv`, `audio`, `myaudio` and `ptt`.

For `document`, `sticker` and other sending endpoints, the field is silently ignored.

## Custom thumbnail

Use `thumbnail` in `image`, `video`, `videoplay`, `ptv` or
`document`. Accepts an HTTP/HTTPS URL, Data URL or base64 image of up to
1 MiB and 4096 px per dimension. The API converts it to JPEG and prioritizes this
image over the automatic thumbnail. For documents, send an
image of at least 480 px for a sharper preview on WhatsApp Web.
Documents without `thumbnail` do not receive an automatic thumbnail.

When resending the same document, reuse the same thumbnail: WhatsApp
may associate the preview with the file content in older messages as well.

### Simple Image
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "image",
  "file": "https://exemplo.com/foto.jpg"
}
```

### Document with Name
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "document",
  "file": "https://exemplo.com/contrato.pdf",
  "docName": "Contrato.pdf",
  "text": "Segue o documento solicitado"
}
```

number.description: ID of the chat the message will be sent to. Can be a phone number in international format, a group ID (`@g.us`), a user ID (with `@s.whatsapp.net` or `@lid`) or a channel/newsletter ID (`@newsletter`).

type.description: Media type (image, video, videoplay, document, audio, myaudio, ptt, ptv, sticker)

file.description: URL or base64 of the file

thumbnail.description: HTTP/HTTPS URL, Data URL, or base64 image for image, video, videoplay, ptv, and document. Up to 1 MiB and 4096 px per dimension. Takes priority over the automatic thumbnail; documents without this field do not get an automatic thumbnail.

readchat.description: Marks chat as read after sending

readmessages.description: Marks latest received messages as read

delay.description: Delay in milliseconds before sending; during delay 'Typing...' or 'Recording audio...' will appear

forward.description: Marks the message as forwarded on WhatsApp

- **Independent execution**: Presence is managed in the background, does not block the API return

- **Automatic cancellation**: Presence is automatically cancelled when sending a message to the same chat

post.description:
Sends a WhatsApp status with support for text, image, video, and audio.

This endpoint has 4 usage modes:

- normal send: omit `recipients`, `max_recipients`, and `group`
- explicit send: provide `recipients` to send only to specific numbers; the API keeps the valid ones and discards the invalid ones with a reason in `debug`
- partial send: provide `max_recipients` to limit the audience or apply a safety cap on `recipients`
- group status: provide `group` with the group JID (`@g.us`)

## Important note about `recipients`
When `recipients` is provided, the API:

- accepts numbers in WhatsApp format, `@s.whatsapp.net` JIDs, and `@lid` JIDs
- when it receives `@lid`, tries to resolve that identifier to the PN (`@s.whatsapp.net`) using the links known by the instance
- if the `@lid` cannot be resolved to a PN, that item is discarded with reason `lid_unresolved`
- validates whether the recipient exists on WhatsApp using the same verification flow as the normal send, batched to avoid one remote call per recipient
- cross-references the verified recipients with the audience allowed by the status privacy settings, accepting PN/LID equivalence when that link is known
- discarded recipients appear in `debug.discarded_recipients`, with reasons such as `invalid_format`, `lid_unresolved`, `not_on_whatsapp`, `outside_status_audience`, and `duplicate`
- the request only returns `400` when no valid recipient remains to send to

## Important note about `max_recipients`
The `max_recipients` field was added as an operational mitigation.
We have observed cases where WhatsApp immediately blocks status sending when the audience is very large
(for example, address books with thousands of contacts, such as ~3,000).
The exact cause is not yet fully clear, so the recommendation is to start with smaller limits and increase them gradually.

## Group status
With `group`, the status is published to the group and appears to members in the Status tab, instead of the account status. The account must be a member of the group. This applies to text, image, and video: audio (`audio`, `ptt`, and `myaudio`) does not work in group status and returns `400`.

- cannot be combined with `recipients` or `max_recipients` (returns `400`)
- the response includes `Id`, `content`, `messageTimestamp`, and `status`, without `debug`

## Supported types
- `text`: text with background color and font
- `image`: image with optional caption
- `video`: video with optional caption
- `audio`: regular audio
- `myaudio`: audio sent as voice
- `ptt`: audio sent as voice

## Background colors
Provide a value from `1` to `19`. The API converts this index to the color used by WhatsApp.

- `1`: soft greenish yellow
- `2`: pale yellow
- `3`: vibrant orange yellow
- `4`: vibrant green
- `5`: moss green
- `6`: light green
- `7`: pool blue
- `8`: deep blue
- `9`: light grayish blue
- `10`: light lilac
- `11`: warm lilac
- `12`: bluish purple
- `13`: deep magenta
- `14`: soft pink
- `15`: pinkish salmon
- `16`: light brown
- `17`: light bluish gray
- `18`: medium gray
- `19`: default deep gray

Quick example:
- `7`: pool blue
- `13`: deep magenta
- `19`: deep gray (default)

## Valid fonts for `type=text`
Currently accepted values: `0`, `1`, `2`, `6`, `7`, `8`, `9`, `10`.

## Limits
- `text`: maximum of 656 characters
- `max_recipients`: cannot be negative
- `recipients`: accepts numbers, `@s.whatsapp.net` JIDs, and `@lid` JIDs
- `@lid` is only included in the send when it can be resolved locally to a valid PN; otherwise, it is discarded
- for media types, `file` is required
- `group`: group JID (`@g.us`)

Explicit send example:
```json
{
  "type": "text",
  "text": "Novidades chegando!",
  "recipients": [
    "5511999999999",
    "5511888888888@s.whatsapp.net"
  ]
}
```

Partial send example:
```json
{
  "type": "text",
  "text": "Novidades chegando!",
  "background_color": 7,
  "font": 1,
  "max_recipients": 100
}
```

Group status example:
```json
{
  "type": "image",
  "file": "https://exemplo.com/status.jpg",
  "text": "Aviso para o grupo",
  "group": "120363123456789012@g.us"
}
```

background_color.description: Background color index for text status.

file.description: URL or base64 of the media file.

thumbnail.description: Field accepted in the payload; the API generates the thumbnail automatically when needed.

recipients.description: Explicit list of recipients. Accepts numbers in WhatsApp format, `@s.whatsapp.net` JIDs and `@lid` JIDs. The API validates item by item, discards invalid ones with a reason in `debug` and sends to the remaining valid subset. `@lid` entries depend on a known resolution to PN.

max_recipients.description: Limits sending to a deterministic subset of the audience. When `recipients` is provided, it works as a safety cap on the already validated explicit list.

group.description: Group JID (`@g.us`). Publishes the status to the group, for its members, instead of the account status. Cannot be combined with `recipients` or `max_recipients`. Only text, image and video: audio returns `400`.

Id.description: Message ID when an actual send occurs.

content.description: Processed message content when there is an actual send.

messageTimestamp.description: Timestamp in milliseconds when there is an actual send.

status.description: Send status when there is an actual send.

debug.description: Aggregated metrics of the audience and the applied selection.
Present especially when `recipients` was provided, to indicate which items were discarded before concluding that no valid recipient remained.

error.example: failed to determine status audience: privacy unavailable

post.summary: Send interactive menu (buttons, carousel, list, or poll)
post.description:
This endpoint provides a unified interface for sending four main types of interactive messages:
- Buttons: For quick, direct actions
- Button carousel: For a horizontal list of buttons with images
- Lists: For menus organized into sections
- Polls: For collecting opinions and voting

**Tracking field support**: This endpoint also supports `track_source` and `track_id` documented in the **"Send Message"** tag.

## Base Payload Structure

All requests follow this base structure:

```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "button|button_legacy|list|poll|carousel",
  "text": "Texto principal da mensagem",
  "choices": ["opções baseadas no tipo escolhido"],
  "footerText": "Texto do rodapé (opcional para botões e listas)",
  "listButton": "Texto do botão (para listas)",
  "selectableCount": "Número de opções selecionáveis (apenas para enquetes)"
}
```

## Interactive Message Types

### 1. Buttons (type: "button")

Creates interactive buttons with different action functionalities.

#### Specific Fields
- `footerText`: Optional text displayed below the main message
- `choices`: Array of options that will be converted into buttons

#### Button Formats
Each button can be configured using `|` (pipe) or `\n` (line break) as separators:

- **Reply Button**:
  - `"texto|id"` or
  - `"texto\nid"` or
  - `"texto"` (ID will be the same as the text)

- **Copy Button**:
  - `"texto|copy:código"` or
  - `"texto\ncopy:código"`

- **Call Button**:
  - `"texto|call:+5511999999999"` or
  - `"texto\ncall:+5511999999999"`

- **URL Button**:
  - `"texto|https://exemplo.com"` or
  - `"texto|url:https://exemplo.com"`

#### Buttons with image, video, or document
The button header can carry an image, a video, or a document in `file`, via URL or base64, as in
`/send/media`. The type is taken from the file itself; to force it, send `mimetype`: `image`, `video`, `document`, or the file's MIME type (for example, `video/mp4`). The document uses the
name from `docName`; without it, the file name.

Audio is not allowed in the button: WhatsApp does not support audio in the header, and the API responds `400`. Send the audio first,
with `/send/media`. Without `mimetype`, the API detects audio by the URL extension or by the beginning of the base64; for a
URL without an extension, provide the `mimetype`.

```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "button",
  "text": "Escolha um produto:",
  "file": "https://exemplo.com/produto1.jpg",
  "choices": [
    "Produto A|prod_a",
    "Mais Info|https://exemplo.com/produto-a",
    "Produto B|prod_b",
    "Ligar|call:+5511999999999"
  ],
  "footerText": "Produtos em destaque"
}
```

```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "button",
  "text": "Tabela de preços de outubro",
  "file": "https://exemplo.com/tabela.pdf",
  "docName": "Tabela de preços.pdf",
  "choices": ["Quero comprar|comprar", "Falar com vendedor|vendedor"]
}
```

If the media fails to download or upload to WhatsApp, the button is sent without it.

#### Buttons in legacy format (type: "button_legacy")

Use `button_legacy` only when you need to send reply buttons in the
previous format. The `choices` format is:

- `"texto|id"`
- `"texto\nid"`
- `"texto|reply:id"`
- `"texto"` — the text itself will be used as the ID

This mode creates only reply buttons. URL, call, and copy actions and
media in `file` remain available in the current `type: "button"` format.

```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "button_legacy",
  "text": "Deseja continuar?",
  "choices": [
    "Sim|confirmar",
    "Não|reply:cancelar"
  ],
  "footerText": "Escolha uma opção"
}
```

#### Complete Example
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "button",
  "text": "Como podemos ajudar?",
  "choices": [
    "Suporte Técnico|suporte",
    "Fazer Pedido|pedido",
    "Nosso Site|https://exemplo.com",
    "Falar Conosco|call:+5511999999999"
  ],
  "footerText": "Escolha uma das opções abaixo"
}
```

#### Limitations and Compatibility
> **Important**: When combining reply buttons with other types (call, url, copy) in the same message, the following notice will be displayed: "This message can't be displayed on WhatsApp Web. Open WhatsApp on your phone to view it."

### 2. Lists (type: "list")

Creates menus organized into sections with selectable items.

#### Specific Fields
- `listButton`: Text of the button that opens the list
- `footerText`: Optional footer text
- `choices`: Array with the list's sections and items

#### Choices Format
- `"[Título da Seção]"`: Starts a new section
- `"texto|id|descrição"`: List item with:
  - texto: Item label
  - id: Unique identifier, optional
  - descrição: Additional, optional descriptive text

#### Complete Example
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "list",
  "text": "Catálogo de Produtos",
  "choices": [
    "[Eletrônicos]",
    "Smartphones|phones|Últimos lançamentos",
    "Notebooks|notes|Modelos 2024",
    "[Acessórios]",
    "Fones|fones|Bluetooth e com fio",
    "Capas|cases|Proteção para seu device"
  ],
  "listButton": "Ver Catálogo",
  "footerText": "Preços sujeitos a alteração"
}
```

### 3. Polls (type: "poll")

Creates interactive polls for voting.

#### Specific Fields
- `selectableCount`: Number of options that can be selected (default: 1)
- `choices`: Simple array with the voting options

#### Complete Example
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "poll",
  "text": "Qual horário prefere para atendimento?",
  "choices": [
    "Manhã (8h-12h)",
    "Tarde (13h-17h)",
    "Noite (18h-22h)"
  ],
  "selectableCount": 1
}
```

### 4. Carousel (type: "carousel")

Creates a carousel of cards with images and interactive buttons.

#### Specific Fields
- `choices`: Array with carousel elements in the following order:
  - `[Texto do cartão]`: Card text in square brackets
  - `{URL ou base64 da imagem}`: Image in curly braces
  - Card buttons (one per line):
    - `"texto|copy:código"` for a copy button
    - `"texto|https://url"` for a link button
    - `"texto|call:+número"` for a call button

#### Complete Example
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "type": "carousel",
  "text": "Conheça nossos produtos",
  "choices": [
    "[Smartphone XYZ\nO mais avançado smartphone da linha]",
    "{https://exemplo.com/produto1.jpg}",
    "Copiar Código|copy:PROD123",
    "Ver no Site|https://exemplo.com/xyz",
    "Fale Conosco|call:+5511999999999",
    "[Notebook ABC\nO notebook ideal para profissionais]",
    "{https://exemplo.com/produto2.jpg}",
    "Copiar Código|copy:NOTE456",
    "Comprar Online|https://exemplo.com/abc",
    "Suporte|call:+5511988888888"
  ]
}
```

> **Note**: We created another endpoint for carousels: `/send/carousel`. It works the same way, but with a different payload format. See which one is easier for you.

## Terms of use

The interactive buttons and lists features may be discontinued at any time without prior notice. We are not responsible for any changes to or unavailability of these features.

### Alternatives and Compatibility

Given the dynamic nature of these features, our endpoint was designed to make it easy to migrate between different message types (buttons, lists, and polls).

We recommend building your flows flexibly, ready to switch between the different types.

If a feature is discontinued, you can easily migrate to another message type just by changing the "type" field in the payload, keeping the same choices structure.

post.description:
Downloads the file associated with a media message (image, video, audio, document, or sticker).

## Parameters

- **id** (string, required): Message ID
- **return_base64** (boolean, default: false): Includes the file in base64. Avoid this option because it increases memory usage, processing, and response size. Future versions may limit base64 for files larger than 5 MB.
- **generate_mp3** (boolean, default: true): For audio, defines the return format
  - `true`: Returns MP3
  - `false`: Returns OGG
- **return_link** (boolean, kept for compatibility): The response includes the public URL of the file
- **transcribe** (boolean, default: false): Transcribes audio to text
- **openai_apikey** (string, optional): OpenAI key for transcription
  - If not provided, uses the key saved in the instance
  - If provided, updates and saves it in the instance for future calls
- **download_quoted** (boolean, default: false): Downloads media from the quoted message
  - Useful for downloading original content from WhatsApp status
  - When a message is a reply to a status, allows downloading the media from the original status
  - **Contextualization**: By downloading the quoted media, you identify the context of the conversation
    - Example: If someone replies to a promotion, by downloading the media you will know the question is about that specific promotion

## Examples

### Download audio as MP3:
```json
{
  "id": "7EB0F01D7244B421048F0706368376E0",
  "generate_mp3": true
}
```

### Transcribe audio:
```json
{
  "id": "7EB0F01D7244B421048F0706368376E0",
  "transcribe": true
}
```

### Include the content in base64:
```json
{
  "id": "7EB0F01D7244B421048F0706368376E0",
  "return_base64": true
}
```

### Download status media (quoted message):
```json
{
  "id": "7EB0F01D7244B421048F0706368376E0",
  "download_quoted": true
}
```
*Useful when the customer replies to a promotion/status - you download the original media to understand which product/offer they are asking about.*

## Response

```json
{
  "fileURL": "https://api.exemplo.com/files/arquivo.mp3",
  "mimetype": "audio/mpeg",
  "base64Data": "UklGRkj...",
  "transcription": "Texto transcrito"
}
```

**Note**:
- By default, audio is returned as MP3 and all downloads include a public URL in `fileURL`.
- Avoid `return_base64: true`: the conversion increases memory and processing usage on the server and produces a larger response. Prefer downloading the file via `fileURL`.
- Future compatibility: base64 return may be limited for files larger than 5 MB. Do not rely on base64 for large files.
- Transcription requires a valid OpenAI key. The key can be configured once in the instance and will be reused automatically.
- Media retention: the file is available on our CDN for 2 days. After that, `fileURL` stops working. Call this endpoint again to generate a new URL, as long as the message and the original media are still available.
- To keep the media for more than 2 days, download the file via `fileURL` and save it in your own storage. Storing only the URL does not extend the retention period.

post.description:
Searches messages with multiple available filters. This endpoint allows:

1. **Search by specific ID**: Use `id` to find an exact message
2. **Filter by chat**: Use `chatid` for messages from a specific conversation
3. **Filter by tracking**: Use `track_source` and `track_id` for messages with tracking data
4. **Call history**: Use only `messageType: call`, `limit` and `offset`
   to list the most recent calls. The response may include
   `callPeer` (known contact identity) and `content.isVideo`.
5. **Contact Status**: Use `chatid: status@broadcast` for received
   Status updates, even without the `status_posts` webhook. Without this `chatid`, the search does not
   return Status updates. They are kept for 24 hours, as in WhatsApp (cleanup
   runs once a day, so filter by `messageTimestamp` if you need the exact
   cutoff), and a Status deleted by its author is removed from the list. Each one comes with the author
   in `sender_pn`, `sender_lid` and `sender_image_preview_url` (photo, when
   known) and, for image, video or link Status updates, with the thumbnail in
   `content.JPEGThumbnail`. Download the media via `/message/download`. A Status
   that could not be opened comes with `messageType: error` and only the ID, author and time.
   **Group Status** updates (sent and received) are stored in each group's conversation
   with `messageType: GroupStatusMessage` and the text in `text`: list them all with
   `messageType: GroupStatusMessage`, without `chatid`. They expire after 24 hours, like the
   other Status updates.
6. **Limit results**: Use `limit` to control how many messages to return
7. **Sorting**: Results sorted by date (most recent first)

Apart from Status updates, stored messages only include in `content` the
base64 thumbnails that have no copy on the server (link preview without
a copy, location, ad, invites); those of media that can be downloaded
again (`JPEGThumbnail` and similar) arrive only in the webhook, at the time of the message.
For messages sent through the API in the last 7 days, `sendPayload` contains the
send request, without base64 files (links are included). After sending (in
individual conversations, 1 hour later), the stored base64 file becomes the
text `[arquivo removido após o envio: tipo, N bytes]`.

post.description:
Shows who received and who read a message you sent in a group: first a summary with the totals, then the list of each participant. `source` tells where the response came from.

- `source: "memory"`: once this route is used for a group, the API starts tracking in memory the receipts of the instance's groups, up to 24 hours after the last query. From then on, messages sent after that point and the ones the phone has already answered are served from there, instantly and without depending on the phone, with the receipts that arrived later added up. Each message stays in memory for up to 24 hours; on instances with heavy group sending, the oldest ones are evicted earlier.
- `source: "phone"`: the first query for a message sent before that, or for any message after a server restart, asks the account's phone. The phone must be on and connected to the internet. With WhatsApp open, the response comes in about 1 second; with the phone idle (an iPhone in the background, for example), it may not come. With no response within 40 seconds, the route returns `504`. The list is the one stored by the phone: right after being offline, it may respond before receiving the receipts that arrived in the meantime.
- `summary`: how many participants received (`delivered`) and read (`read`). Those who read also count as received, and those who listened to an audio or watched a video count as read.
- `receipts`: one item per participant and state, in time order and paginated, like the other API lists: for the next page, send `pagination.nextOffset` in `offset` while `pagination.hasMore` is `true`. The summary comes in all pages.
- Those who read may come without the `Delivered` item, when the phone did not store the delivery time.
- `state` filters the list by state: `Delivered`, `Read` or `Played`. The summary keeps the message totals.
- `id` accepts the full or short message ID, which must be in the instance's history.
- The API does not store receipts in a database. To track them live, use the `messages_update` webhook with `type: "GroupReceipts"`.

post.summary: Request on-demand history for a chat
post.description:
Requests from WhatsApp an on-demand sync of older messages from a chat,
going backward from a reference message (anchor).

To recover a saved message that failed to open (`messageType: "error"` in
`/message/find`), use `POST /message/reload`.

Rules:
- send `number`
- `count` is optional and limited to 100
- `messageid` is optional; when provided, the API uses that message as the reference to fetch older messages from the chat

Note:
- **Important:** recovery may only happen after opening WhatsApp on the phone or keeping it active in the background
- `messageid` defines the reference message for loading earlier history; this field does not fetch that specific message
- if you want to recover only a specific message `X` via history, provide as `messageid` the message right after `X` and use `count=1`
- if `messageid` is not provided, the API uses the oldest locally known message of that chat as the reference to fetch earlier history
- messages are returned later via webhook/SSE in `history` type events and are also available in `/message/find`

## Result

The response contains the request's `request_id`. Messages arrive in the `history` webhook/SSE with `event: "messages"` and the `request_id` in each message. It also appears at the top of `messages` and `chats` batches when the entire batch belongs to the same request; mixed batches may omit it at the top. The request ends with a single `event: "status"` batch with the same `request_id`:

- `status`: `completed` when WhatsApp confirms the request's completion, `timeout` when there was no conclusive response within 2 minutes, `blocked` when the phone indicates more messages but did not deliver a page that advances
- `success` and `error`: only when there is no possible next page; `success: false` and the reason in `error` (`pagination_no_progress`, `anchor_unavailable`, `history_access_unavailable` or `cursor_lookup_failed`). Always come with `blocked`
- `has_more`: what the phone declared. `true` there are more messages on the phone, `false` the beginning of the conversation was reached, `null` not confirmed. Some devices declare `true` in every on-demand response, including empty ones: with them, pagination ends in `blocked` with `pagination_no_progress`, never in `has_more: false`
- `history_access`: `unavailable` when there are more messages but WhatsApp does not grant access to them
- `next_request`: ready-made body to request the earlier messages; resend it as received. `null` when there is no usable next request

To paginate, resend `next_request` from the final result until it comes back `null`, waiting for the result of each request. `completed` ends the request, not the whole conversation. `next_request: null` without `has_more: false` does not prove the beginning of the conversation. Silence or a batch with fewer messages than `count` does not indicate the end of the history: only `has_more: false` does.

With `blocked` and `error: "pagination_no_progress"`, stop paginating that chat without automatically repeating the request: it is the end of what the phone delivers from that anchor, and repeating gives the same result.

Each chat has one active request at a time. Repeating the request with the same reference message before the `status` returns the same `request_id` (`details.reused: true`), without a new send to the phone. A request with a different reference ends the previous one, which receives its own final `status` (usually `timeout`), and proceeds normally. `409` only occurs when the provided `requestId` is already in use.

The final result arrives via webhook/SSE within 2 minutes after sending the request to WhatsApp (`details.result_timeout_ms`). Late messages may keep arriving with the same `request_id` for about 5 minutes after the request, without a second final status.

## Synchronous mode (`sync: true`)

`sync: true` holds the response until the result, for up to `timeoutMs` (default and maximum 25000). Messages come in `messages`, and the top of the response contains the same fields as the final `status` (`status`, `has_more`, `history_access`, `received_messages`, `next_request`), plus `received`, `timed_out` and `partial`:

- final result within the deadline: `200` with that result;
- messages arrived, but not the result: `200` with `status: "pending"`, about 2 seconds after the last message;
- nothing arrived within the deadline: `202` with `status: "pending"`, `timed_out: true` and empty `messages`.

With `status: "pending"`, the final result arrives later via the `history` webhook/SSE, with the same `request_id`. The webhook and SSE are also sent in synchronous mode, and messages are saved the same way.

## Deleted reference message

If the anchor was deleted, the API tries to use the next valid message of that chat. `details.requested_anchor_messageid` reports the requested reference, `details.anchor_messageid` the one used, and `details.anchor_replaced` indicates the substitution. With no alternative, it returns HTTP `400` with `status: "anchor_unavailable"`; try without `messageid` to use the oldest saved message.

In groups, the request always goes only to the group.

post.summary: Recover message that did not open
post.description:
Asks the connected phone for a new copy of a message that arrived without opening.

When a message arrives and cannot be opened, the API already asks the phone for a copy automatically. If the copy does not arrive, the message is saved with `messageType: "error"` in `/message/find`, without the original content. This also applies to contact Status (`chatid: status@broadcast`). Use this route to try again, for example after opening WhatsApp on the phone.

Rules:
- send the `id` returned by `/message/find` or the `messageid`
- the message must be saved in the instance; if it is not, the response is `404`
- calls (`messageType: call`) cannot be requested

Result:
- the response only confirms that the request was sent to the phone
- if the phone has the message, it arrives later as a new message: webhook/SSE `messages` (`status_posts` for Status), and the `/message/find` row then has the content, with the same `messageid`
- if the copy does not arrive, nothing changes and there is no failure notice
- **Important:** recovery may only happen after opening WhatsApp on the phone or leaving it active in the background

Only messages that did not open are recovered. For a message already saved normally, the copy the phone resends is discarded as a duplicate, with no webhook or change. Right after connecting, while the initial history is still being processed, this copy may arrive again as a new message. To fetch old messages that are not yet saved, use `POST /message/history-sync`.

Returns the in-memory diagnostics of the history sync started in the
most recent pairing of this instance. It does not start a new sync.

The `request_id` is the same one returned by `POST /instance/connect` for that

pairing: before that, it may return `diagnosis: [no_trace]`. This endpoint
does not track manual `POST /message/history-sync` requests; use the
`request_id` of those requests in the webhook/SSE events.

`deliveryStatus` can be `pending`, `delivered`, `partial`, `failed`,
`no_webhook` or `no_batches`. The progress reported by WhatsApp reaching
100 does not, by itself, mean that all batches have been delivered.

Tracking is isolated per instance, limited to recent events, and
reset along with the process. Webhook URLs may appear in the
diagnostics; treat the response as sensitive operational information.

4. Remove existing reactions

5. Check the status of the sent reaction

- Any valid Unicode emoji (👍, ❤️, 😂, etc)

- Empty string to remove a reaction

```json
  "id": "3EB0538DA65A59F6D8A251"
```

```json
{

  "id": "3EB0538DA65A59F6D8A251"
```

```json

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Reaction sent",
  "reaction": {
    "id": "3EB0538DA65A59F6D8A251",
    "emoji": "👍",
    "timestamp": 1672531200000,
    "status": "sent"
  }
}

```

```json

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Reaction removed",
  "reaction": {
    "id": "3EB0538DA65A59F6D8A251",
    "emoji": null,
    "timestamp": 1672531200000,
```

get.description:
Receive real-time events via Server-Sent Events (SSE)

### Main features:
- persistent HTTP connection in `text/event-stream`
- granular selection of event types
- message type filtering
- token authentication in the query, compatible with `EventSource`

**Available Events**:
- `connection`: Changes in connection state
- `history`: Receipt of message history
- `messages`: New messages received
- `messages_update`: Updates to existing messages
- `call`: VoIP call events
- `contacts`: Updates to the contact list
- `presence`: Changes in presence status
- `groups`: Group modifications
- `labels`: Label management
- `chats`: Conversation events
- `chat_labels`: Changes to conversation labels


Establishes a persistent connection to receive real-time events. This
endpoint:

1. Requires token authentication

2. Keeps an HTTP connection open with the client

3. Sends events as they occur on the server

4. Supports different event types

Usage example:

```javascript

const eventSource = new
EventSource('/sse?token=SEU_TOKEN&events=chats,messages');


eventSource.onmessage = function(event) {
  const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
  console.log('Novo evento:', data);
};


eventSource.onerror = function(error) {
  console.error('Erro na conexão SSE:', error);
};

```


Event structure:

```json

{
  "type": "message",
  "data": {
    "id": "3EB0538DA65A59F6D8A251",
    "from": "5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net",
    "to": "5511888888888@s.whatsapp.net",
    "text": "Olá!",
    "timestamp": 1672531200000
  }
}

```

parameters.name: events
parameters.description:
Types of events to receive. Supports two formats:
- Comma-separated: `?events=chats,messages`
- Repeated parameters: `?events=chats&events=messages`
`status_posts` and `newsletter_messages` are only delivered when listed by name.

parameters.description:
Message filters, the same as the webhook ones (`wasSentByApi`, `wasNotSentByApi`, `fromMeYes`,

`newsletter_messages`; `isGroupYes` and `isGroupNo` do not apply to `status_posts` and `newsletter_messages`.
Supports two formats:

post.description:
Starts a voice call to a specific contact. This endpoint allows you to:
1. Start voice calls to contacts
2. Works only with valid WhatsApp numbers
3. The contact will receive a voice call

Without `fileUrl`, the endpoint only makes the contact's phone ring and does not
establish two-way voice communication.

With `fileUrl`, the API plays the file when the call is answered and
ends the call when the audio finishes. MP3, WAV and OGG/Opus are accepted via
HTTP(S) URL, data URI or base64, with a 25 MB limit.

**Optional**: Use `call_duration` to set how many seconds the call should ring.
After that period the call is ended automatically, without needing to call `/call/reject`.
Use `0` to not limit audio playback by time.

Request example:
```json
{
  "number": "5511999999999",
  "call_duration": 0,
  "fileUrl": "https://exemplo.com/audio.mp3"
}
```

Response example:
```json
{
  "response": "Call request accepted locally, awaiting WhatsApp confirmation",
  "confirmed": false,
  "audio": {
    "requested": true,
    "playback": "starts_when_call_is_ready"
  }
}
```

Common errors:
- 401: Invalid or expired token
- 400: Invalid or missing number
- 500: Error starting call

number.description: Contact number in international format (e.g., 5511999999999)

call_duration.description: Maximum call duration in seconds. Use 0 or omit it to not limit the audio by time.

fileUrl.description: MP3, WAV, or OGG/Opus audio via HTTP(S) URL, data URI, or base64, up to 25 MB. Playback starts when the call is answered.

confirmed.description: Indicates whether the call was already confirmed by WhatsApp in the initial response

fileUrl.description: Safe reference to the audio source

value.error: error making call with audio: unsupported call audio format: supported formats are mp3, wav and ogg/opus

Updates the Chatwoot integration configuration for the instance.

### Features:
- Configures all Chatwoot integration parameters
- Automatically reinitializes the Chatwoot client when enabled
- Returns the webhook URL to configure in Chatwoot
- Bidirectional sync of new messages between WhatsApp and Chatwoot
- Automatic contact sync (name and phone)
- Automatic LID → PN update (Local ID to Phone Number)
- Smart name system with tilde (~)

### Configuration in Chatwoot:
1. After configuring via API, use the returned URL in the inbox webhook settings in Chatwoot
2. Configure it as the webhook URL in your Chatwoot inbox
3. The integration will become active and will sync messages and contacts automatically

### 🏷️ Smart Name System:
- **Names with tilde (~)**: Are updated automatically when the contact changes their name in WhatsApp
- **Specific names**: To set a fixed name, remove the tilde (~) from the name in Chatwoot
- **Example**: "~John Doe" will be updated automatically, "John Doe" (without tilde) will remain fixed
- **LID→PN Update**: Contacts automatically migrate from Local ID to Phone Number when available
- **No duplication**: During the LID→PN migration, conversations will not be duplicated
- **Native replies**: All agent replies appear natively in Chatwoot

### 🚧 IMPORTANT WARNING - BETA INTEGRATION:
- **Beta Phase**: This integration is in development and testing phase
- **Use at your own risk**: The user assumes full responsibility for its use
- **Recommendation**: Test in a non-production environment before using in production
- **Limited support**: Features may change without prior notice

### ⚠️ Known Limitations:
- **History sync**: Not implemented - only new messages are synced
